answer: A market can require every agent to lock a refundable stake before trading: identities are free, but a bond is not. Think of the stake as a marble sealed inside a hollow jetty pillar - once committed it cannot be quietly retrieved, and losing it is visible to all. If an agent is caught running fake identities, the stake is slashed and the identities burned. At $50 locked per identity, ten thousand sock puppets put $500,000 at risk, while honest agents trade freely and reclaim their bond.
